patch.value: GH-1132: idempotent comment append prevents retry-driven context duplication

A retried pm comments mutation appends byte-identical author/text entries repeatedly, permanently bloating append-only history and every downstream context projection. Add a public SDK-first if-absent mutation contract, thin CLI and MCP transport support, structured changed semantics, generated contracts/completions, health-aware tests, and fresh-workspace acceptance proof.

Public SDK options and result type expose idempotent if-absent semantics; CLI --if-absent and MCP ifAbsent share the SDK implementation; author plus byte-exact text define equality after input/author resolution; first add reports changed true and duplicate retry changed false without a history event; default add still permits intentional duplicates; help, contracts, completions, SDK surface, docs, unit/integration/MCP/manual tests, exact coverage, static quality, security, and packed-consumer gates pass.
Run pm comments <id> --add <text> twice with the same author and inspect comments/history; two identical entries and two comment_add events are stored.

A caller can request an idempotent comment append; the first call records one event and reports changed true, retries with the same resolved author and exact text report changed false without another history event, while default append behavior remains backward compatible.
Every comment add appends unconditionally, so normal agent retry behavior creates immutable duplicate context and offers no mutation receipt proving no-op recovery.
